subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: At dynamic equilibrium across a membrane during diffusion:
options: molecules continue to move in both directions but there is no net movement
molecules move only from low to high concentration
questions.explain: At equilibrium molecules still move randomly both ways, but with equal rates so there is no net change in concentration.

questions.q: Two cells are in contact: cell A has a water potential of -400 kPa and cell B has -750 kPa. Water will move:
options: from cell A to cell B
not at all because the cells are isolated
from cell B to cell A
in both directions equally with no net movement
questions.explain: Water moves from a higher (less negative) water potential to a lower (more negative) one, i.e. from A (-400) to B (-750).

questions.q: A student tests a solution with Benedict's reagent and observes no colour change on heating, then performs the Benedict's test again after boiling with dilute acid and neutralising, obtaining a brick-red precipitate. This indicates:
options: a non-reducing sugar such as sucrose was present
a reducing sugar was present originally
questions.explain: Acid hydrolysis breaks a non-reducing sugar into reducing monosaccharides, which then give a positive Benedict's result.

questions.q: A person with blood group AB has the genotype:
questions.explain: Group AB results from codominant alleles IA and IB both being expressed.

questions.q: What is the function of tRNA during translation?
options: To bring specific amino acids to the ribosome according to its anticodon
To carry the genetic code from the nucleus to the ribosome
To unwind the DNA double helix
questions.explain: Each tRNA carries a specific amino acid and pairs its anticodon with the complementary mRNA codon.

questions.q: In semi-conservative replication, each new DNA molecule consists of:
options: One original strand and one new strand
Fragments of both original strands recombined
questions.explain: Each daughter molecule conserves one parental strand which acts as a template for one newly synthesised strand.

questions.q: Discontinuous variation differs from continuous variation because it:
options: Falls into distinct, non-overlapping categories controlled by one or few genes
Is always caused by the environment
questions.explain: Discontinuous variation gives discrete categories, typically controlled by one or a few genes with little environmental effect.

questions.q: A property of water that makes it an effective coolant in transpiration and sweating is its:
options: inability to act as a solvent
questions.explain: Water's high latent heat of vaporisation means much heat energy is removed when it evaporates, providing efficient cooling.

questions.q: Which factor would increase the permeability of a cell membrane?
options: An increase in temperature, increasing phospholipid movement and creating gaps
A decrease in temperature, increasing phospholipid order
questions.explain: Higher temperatures increase phospholipid kinetic energy and fluidity, and can denature membrane proteins, increasing permeability.

questions.q: During transcription, which enzyme joins RNA nucleotides together to form pre-mRNA?
questions.explain: RNA polymerase catalyses the formation of phosphodiester bonds between RNA nucleotides during transcription.

questions.q: In plant cells, water potential is determined by the equation:
options: Psi = solute potential x pressure potential
questions.explain: Water potential equals the (negative) solute potential plus the (usually positive) pressure potential exerted by the cell wall.

questions.q: The ABO blood group system is an example of multiple alleles because:
options: There are more than two alleles in the population for one gene
Each person has more than two alleles
questions.explain: Three alleles (IA, IB, i) exist in the population for the single ABO gene, though each individual carries only two.
